sections.h2: Who to call about your tax bill
sections.html:
Tax Administration is in the Smithfield courthouse at 207 East Johnston Street, second floor. Hours are weekdays from 8 to 5, and the office closes on county holidays.

Two phone lines divide the work, as the county contact page shows:

  • 919-989-5120 (Tax Collection): your bill, payment plans, wage garnishment, bank attachment and foreclosure policy. Mail goes to P.O. Box 451, Smithfield, NC 27577.
  • 919-989-5130 (Tax Administration): listing property, valuation and relief programs. Mail goes to P.O. Box 368, Smithfield, NC 27577.

An online portal shows bills, appraisal cards and sales. The county also posts a delinquent tax file and an accounts receivable file on its downloads page, which lenders use.

The county rate is 0.510 per $100 of value for the 2026 tax year, down from 0.520 the year before. The county fire protection service district adds 0.115 on top. If you live inside a town, that town's rate is added too.

The county's full rate chart also has Kenly at 0.650, Princeton at 0.585, Wilson's Mills at 0.500, Pine Level at 0.390, Downtown Smithfield at 0.160, the Moccasin Creek service district at 0.025 and a research and training zone at 0.080. The county GIS decides which districts apply to a parcel. If the districts on your bill look wrong, call 919-989-5130.

Statements are mailed in July and the bill is due September 1. You can pay without penalty through January 5. On January 6 the balance picks up 2 percent, and then three-quarters of a percent more every month.

Billing follows whoever owned the property on January 1, but the paper statement is mailed to the owner of record on June 30. If one shows up for a house you have already sold, hand it to the buyer. Lenders pull their own data from the tax office and usually pay late in the year, so a copy sent to you is just for your files.

Owners who want installments can sign a payment agreement for the current year, accepted until the bill turns delinquent. Older unpaid years are not eligible. Ways to pay:

  • Phone: 888-327-7344, with the year and bill number
  • Web: the county pay taxes page
  • Mail: Tax Collections, P.O. Box 451
  • In person: a locked drop box at the courthouse doors

Cars and trucks are billed separately. The state tag and tax system collects vehicle tax through the Division of Motor Vehicles.

The previous countywide revaluation was in 2019, and the new values took effect January 1, 2025. They drive tax bills from the summer of 2025 until the next countywide revaluation, with exceptions such as new construction.

State law at G.S. 105-286 requires every county to reappraise at least every eight years. The county hired Pearson Appraisal Service, and its own certified appraisers reviewed the results. They used aerial images, street-level images, sales data and the tax database, and made field visits to more than 115,000 properties.

Appraised value and assessed value are the same as of the revaluation date. An online home estimate can differ from the tax office figure because automated models do not check whether a sale meets the statutory test, while the county screens sales by phone calls and visits. A foreclosure sale gets careful analysis before it counts as market evidence, and your own purchase price may differ from market value.

Report changes you make to a property, such as additions, demolished buildings, or fire and flood damage. Email taxoffice@johnstonnc.gov, call 919-989-5130, or note it on the January listing form.

Value appeals follow a yearly calendar. The next window for real property opens in February 2027, and the county's valuation appeal form must be in by the deadline on its appeals page.

Personal property follows a different clock: the form has to reach the tax office within thirty days of the bill date. Individual and business personal property share one form, and both are on the county forms page.

After that review the next body is the equalization and review board, which G.S. 105-322 assigns to the commissioners by default. A last appeal to the state Property Tax Commission is possible under G.S. 105-290, filed with a copy to the assessor.

Listing has its own deadline. January is the listing month, and a late list adds a 10 percent penalty to the levy. Last year's improvements, untagged vehicles, boats, aircraft and business assets all go on the form. A building permit does not count as listing.

The county applies three state homestead programs for 2026, and an owner picks one. File Form AV-9, available from the county forms page, and ask for the relief specialist at 919-989-5130.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: owner is 65, or permanently and totally disabled, and the owner plus spouse have combined income of $38,800 or less.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: same age or disability test, income cap of $58,200, and five years of owning and occupying the home.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: service-connected total and permanent disability, or a specially adapted housing benefit. A surviving spouse who has not remarried can also qualify.

The county wants applications before June 1 of the tax year. Farm, forest and horticultural land can qualify for present use valuation, which is a separate program filed on Form AV-5 during January listing. A tract removed from that program owes the deferred tax for the current year plus three earlier years, with interest. Builders can apply every January to exclude inventory value, for as long as three years on homes and five on commercial lots.

Nothing is divided for you. The county does not split or prorate a bill between buyer and seller, so the two of you settle it by contract, through the broker or the closing attorney. When a transfer happens mid-year the seller stays responsible for the bill, and any credit at closing is a private deal.

If you owe earlier years, ask collections for a payoff figure before closing. G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien to the parcel from the listing date, so the buyer's title company will want it cleared.

A sensible order of steps:

  1. Call 919-989-5120 and request the balance for every open year.
  2. Ask your closing attorney to pay the balance from your proceeds.
  3. Confirm the current-year bill and how the contract splits it.
  4. Forward any statement that arrives after closing to the buyer.

If an account stays unpaid, the county sends notices and a pre-foreclosure letter, then gives the file to a private attorney. Auctions are held on the courthouse steps, usually from about ten in the morning, and the winning bidder deposits 5 percent. The sale is not final for ten days, and any upset bid must beat the previous one by 5 percent or $750, whichever is greater. Until the court confirms the sale, you can redeem the parcel by paying the taxes, interest and costs.

A cash sale skips the listing, showings and buyer financing, but the tax lien still has to be paid at or before closing.

The county seat is Smithfield, and the population is 256,448, up 18.7 percent from 2020. There are about 99,408 housing units, owners live in 76.1 percent of households, and the typical owner-held home is worth $305,600. New building permits numbered 3,002 in 2025, so new construction competes with resales. Clayton, Selma, Benson, Four Oaks and other towns each levy their own rate in addition to the county's.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 tax rate for Johnston County?
faqs.a: The county levies 0.510 per $100 for 2026, down from 0.520 in 2025. The fire protection district adds 0.115, and each town adds its own rate.

faqs.q: When do Johnston County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: They turn delinquent after January 5. Interest begins January 6 at 2 percent for the first month, then three-quarters of a percent per month.

faqs.q: Will Johnston County divide the tax between me and the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The county bills the January 1 owner and does not prorate, so your broker or closing attorney should settle the split on the closing statement.

faqs.q: Can I spread Johnston County taxes over installments?
faqs.a: Yes, for the current year only. Return a payment agreement to collections before the bill goes delinquent, since prior-year balances are not eligible.

faqs.q: Whom do I ask about Johnston County tax relief?
faqs.a: Call 919-989-5130 and ask for a property tax relief specialist. The application is Form AV-9, due before June 1.
